statement.p: Select the trigonometric identity you used in solving this problem.

hint.p: The integral involves \tan u and \sec u where the exponent of \tan u is odd and positive. So we rewrite in order to have a copy of \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) and use a trigonometric identity to turn the remaining even powers of \tan(9 x) into an expression of \sec^2(9 x). Then use u-substitution with u= \sec(9 x).

Thus the integral can be rewritten as \int 5\tan^{3}\mathopen{}\left(9x\right)\sec^{3}\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \, dx = 5 \int \tan^2(9 x) \sec^2(9 x) \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) \, dx = 5 \int \bigg( \sec^2(9 x)-1 \bigg) \sec^2(9 x) \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) \, dx Now let u= \sec(9 x).
Letting u= \sec(9 x) means that du= 9 \sec(9 x)\tan(9 x) \, dx, and thus dx= \frac{du}{9\sec(9 x)\tan(9 x)}.

So the integral turns into = 5 \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) \frac{du}{9\sec(9 x)\tan(9 x)} = \frac{5}{9} \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \, du = \frac{5}{9} \int \bigg( u^4-u^2 \bigg) \, du And each part can be integrated with power rule. Don't forget to plug back in what u equals!

solution.p: The integral involves \tan u and \sec u where the exponent of \tan u is odd and positive. So we rewrite in order to have a copy of \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) and use a trigonometric identity to turn the remaining even powers of \tan(9 x) into an expression of \sec^2(9 x).

Then let u= \sec(9 x), which means that du= 9 \sec(9 x)\tan(9 x) \, dx, and thus dx= \frac{du}{9\sec(9 x)\tan(9 x)}. \begin{aligned} \int 5\tan^{3}\mathopen{}\left(9x\right)\sec^{3}\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \, dx \amp = 5 \int \tan^2(9 x) \sec^2(9 x) \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = 5 \int \bigg( \sec^2(9 x)-1 \bigg) \sec^2(9 x) \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = 5 \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \sec(9 x) \tan(9 x) \frac{du}{9\sec(9 x)\tan(9 x)} \\\\ \amp = \frac{5}{9} \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{5}{9} \int \bigg( u^4-u^2 \bigg) \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{5}{9} \bigg[\frac{ u^5}{5}-\frac{u^3}{3}\bigg]+C \\\\ \amp = \frac{5}{9} \bigg[\frac{ \sec^5(9 x)}{5}-\frac{\sec^3(9 x)}{3}\bigg]+C \end{aligned}
The correct trigonometric identity used is A.
